question: On Earth Day 1990 New York closed 42nd Street to traffic, and officials braced for gridlock. What happened?
options: Midtown traffic seized up for hours
Traffic flowed as well or better
answer: Traffic flowed as well or better. Dietrich Braess showed in 1968 that when each driver takes the quickest route for himself, adding a road can slow everyone, so removing one can speed them up. New York's transport commissioner said many had predicted doomsday. Selfish choices can make a network worse than planned.
move: In a network of selfish choices, more options can make everyone slower.
ask: Which extra option in my life might be making everything slower?
trap: Assuming less road always means more traffic.
source: New York Times news service, The solution to traffic jams: close down a street, 1990
